newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Normandy awaits appeal on Yanacocha.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Normandy awaits appeal on Yanacocha.

text.p: Normandy Mining Ltd is disappointed with a Peruvian court ruling over rights to a stake in the Yanacocha gold mine but is awaiting the outcome of an appeal by its joint venture partner, a spokesman said.
"Normandy has been advised that BRGM (Bureau de Recherches Geoliques et Mineres) will be appealing," Normandy general manager corporate affairs Colin Jackson told Reuters.

Peruvian owned Compania de Minera Buenaventura SA said on Wednesday that it had won a lawsuit allowing it and joint venture partner Newmont Mining Co to exercise pre-emptive rights to buy a 24.7 percent stake, valued by the
court at US$109 million, in Yanacocha.
Newmont and Beuneventura filed the suit to prevent the former French government owned BRGM from transferring the stake to its La Source joint venture with Normandy.
"Of course we are disappointed," Jackson said.
"(However) it is not a setback, it is just part of the process which could easily take several more years," he said.
Jackson said the court valuation of the stake "clearly is a long way from the current market valuation of well in excess of US$1 billion (for the total Yanacocha project)."
However, he said the value was "only relevant if you ultimately lose".
Jackson said the court decision would have no impact on La Source's bottom line as Yanacocha had not been included in any earnings forecasts.
